content.text: Network metrics on seat's connections are close to normal; there is no sustained drop or retransmit pattern. Next I'll compare basic-service and the other changed services against their normal baselines to see whether anything else is independently faulty.

input.query: SELECT 'abn' src, service_name, span_name, count(*) n, round(approx_quantile(duration/1e6,0.95),1) p95, round(avg(duration/1e6),1) avg FROM abnormal_traces WHERE service_name IN ('ts-basic-service','ts-travel-service','ts-travel2-service') AND span_name IN ('POST','GET','POST /api/v1/basicservice/basic/travels','POST /api/v1/travelservice/trips/left') GROUP BY 1,2,3 UNION ALL SELECT 'nor', service_name, span_name, count(*), round(approx_quantile(duration/1e6,0.95),1), round(avg(duration/1e6),1) FROM normal_traces WHERE service_name IN ('ts-basic-service','ts-travel-service','ts-travel2-service') AND span_name IN ('POST','GET','POST /api/v1/basicservice/basic/travels','POST /api/v1/travelservice/trips/left') GROUP BY 1,2,3 ORDER BY 2,3,1

content.text: Basic-service's own time has also grown, so I'll check its child calls and its container metrics to see whether it's a second independent fault or just affected by load.

input.query: SELECT 'abn' src, c.service_name, c.span_name, count(*) n, round(approx_quantile(c.duration/1e6,0.95),1) p95 FROM abnormal_traces p JOIN abnormal_traces c ON c.parent_span_id=p.span_id AND c.trace_id=p.trace_id WHERE p.service_name='ts-basic-service' GROUP BY 1,2,3 UNION ALL SELECT 'nor', c.service_name, c.span_name, count(*), round(approx_quantile(c.duration/1e6,0.95),1) FROM normal_traces p JOIN normal_traces c ON c.parent_span_id=p.span_id AND c.trace_id=p.trace_id WHERE p.service_name='ts-basic-service' GROUP BY 1,2,3 ORDER BY 3,1

SELECT 'abn' src, service_name, metric, round(avg(value),3) v FROM abnormal_metrics WHERE service_name IN ('ts-basic-service','ts-travel-service','ts-preserve-service') AND metric IN ('container.cpu.usage','container.memory.working_set','jvm.cpu.recent_utilization','k8s.container.restarts','k8s.pod.uptime') GROUP BY 1,2,3 UNION ALL SELECT 'nor', service_name, metric, round(avg(value),3) FROM normal_metrics WHERE service_name IN ('ts-basic-service','ts-travel-service','ts-preserve-service') AND metric IN ('container.cpu.usage','container.memory.working_set','jvm.cpu.recent_utilization','k8s.container.restarts','k8s.pod.uptime') GROUP BY 1,2,3 ORDER BY 2,3,1

content.text: Basic-service's own time is modest and its callees are only slightly slower, so it looks like a knock-on effect rather than a separate fault. Last check: whether seat-service normally has any child spans, which decides between a method-level and a database-level fault.

input.query: SELECT p.span_name, count(*) parents, sum(CASE WHEN c.span_id IS NULL THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) leaf, round(approx_quantile(p.duration/1e6,0.95),1) p95_parent_ms, round(approx_quantile(c.duration/1e6,0.95),1) p95_child_ms FROM normal_traces p LEFT JOIN normal_traces c ON c.parent_span_id=p.span_id AND c.trace_id=p.trace_id WHERE p.service_name='ts-seat-service' GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 2 DESC LIMIT 10

content.text: Normal seat traffic has a child call to config (about 9 ms). In the abnormal window that config call is still fast, so the time is spent inside seat's own method. One last query confirms the caller-to-callee edges along the impact chain.

input.query: SELECT p.service_name caller, c.service_name callee, count(*) n, round(approx_quantile(p.duration/1e6,0.95),1) caller_p95_ms, round(approx_quantile(c.duration/1e6,0.95),1) callee_p95_ms FROM abnormal_traces p JOIN abnormal_traces c ON c.parent_span_id=p.span_id AND c.trace_id=p.trace_id WHERE p.service_name IN ('ts-preserve-service','ts-travel-service','ts-travel-plan-service','ts-route-plan-service','ts-ui-dashboard') AND c.service_name IN ('ts-seat-service','ts-travel-service','ts-route-plan-service','ts-travel-plan-service','ts-preserve-service') AND p.service_name<>c.service_name AND p.kind<>'' GROUP BY 1,2 ORDER BY 4 DESC
